(Section)

On His words: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 1-3]

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is their judgment. Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah – then indeed, the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds. And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do. And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do. And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous. And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah. And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Does not Allah know best what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 1-11]

So let the servant reflect on the context of these verses and the lessons and treasures of wisdom they contain. When messengers are sent to a people, they stand between two matters: either one of them says, "We believe," or he does not say that, but rather persists in evil deeds and disbelief. Whoever says, "We believe," his Lord tests him, tries him and puts him to trial. Fitnah (trial, testing) is affliction and examination, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liar. Whoever does not say, "We believe," let him not think that he can frustrate Allah, escape Him or outpace Him, for he is only folding the stages in His hands.

[Poetry]
And how can a man flee from Him in his sin,
When the stages are being folded in His hands?

Whoever believes in the messengers and obeys them, their enemies oppose him and harm him, so he is afflicted with what pains him. And whoever does not believe in them and does not obey them is punished in this world and the Hereafter, so there comes to him what pains him, and this painful thing is greater in pain and more lasting than the pain of following them. Therefore, every soul that believes or turns away from belief must experience pain. But the believer experiences pain in this world at the outset, and then the good outcome is his in this world and the Hereafter. The one who turns away from belief experiences pleasure at the outset, and then he proceeds to lasting pain.

al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked: Which is better for a man, that he be empowered or that he be tested? He said: He is not empowered until he is tested, and Allah the Exalted tested the Messengers of firm resolve, and when they were patient, He empowered them. So no one should think that he will be free of pain at all. Rather, the people of pain differ in their intellect: the most intelligent of them is the one who sells lasting great pain for brief, passing pain, and the most wretched of them is the one who sells brief, passing pain for lasting great pain.

If it is said: How would a sensible person choose this? It is said: What drives him to this is ready cash versus deferred payment.

And the soul is entrusted with love of what is immediate.
﴿Nay, but you love the immediate and neglect the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 20] ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate and leave behind them a heavy day.﴾ [al-Insan: 27] This occurs to everyone, for man is civil by nature; he must live among people, and people have wills and perceptions, so they ask him to agree with them in them. If he does not agree with them, they harm him and punish him; and if he agrees with them, harm and punishment befall him, sometimes from them and sometimes from others. Like one who has religion and piety who dwells among wicked, oppressive people, who cannot carry out their wickedness and oppression except with his agreement or his silence. If he agrees with them or remains silent, he is safe from their evil at the outset, but then they dominate him with humiliation and harm many times over what he feared at the outset had he denounced them and opposed them. And if he is safe from them, he must still be humiliated and punished at the hands of others. So the utmost prudence lies in acting upon what 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, said to Mu'awiyah:
("Whoever pleases Allah at the displeasure of people, Allah will suffice him against the people's troubles. And whoever pleases people at the displeasure of Allah, the people will not avail him anything against Allah.")

Whoever reflects on the conditions of the world will see this often: among those who help rulers in their corrupt aims, and among those who help people of innovation in their innovations, fleeing from their punishment. Whomever Allah guides, inspires with his right guidance and protects from the evil of his own self, refrains from agreeing to the commission of what is forbidden, and endures their hostility. Then the outcome in this world and the Hereafter is his, just as it was for the Messengers and their followers, such as the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those among the scholars, worshippers, righteous rulers and merchants who were tested, and others.

Since pain is unavoidable in any case, Allah the Glorified consoled whoever chooses brief, passing pain over great, lasting pain with His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah – then indeed, the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 5] So He set a term for the duration of this pain, which must come, and it is the day of meeting Him. Then the servant will delight with the greatest delight in what he bore of pain for His sake and seeking His pleasure, and his delight, joy and gladness will be in proportion to the pain he bore for Allah and for Allah's sake. He emphasized this consolation and solace with hope for meeting Him, so that the servant's longing for the meeting with his Lord and his Protector might carry him through bearing the hardship of immediate pain. Indeed, longing for His meeting may sometimes make him forget witnessing the pain and feeling it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his Lord for longing for His meeting, saying in the supplication narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Hibban: "O Allah, I ask You by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive if life is good for me, and take me when death is good for me. I ask You for fear of You in secret and in public, I ask You for the word of truth in anger and in contentment, I ask You for moderation in poverty and wealth, I ask You for a bounty that does not end, I ask You for coolness of eye that does not cease, I ask You for contentment after decree, I ask You for the coolness of life after death, I ask You for the delight of looking at Your Face, and I ask You for longing for meeting You, without harmful adversity or misleading trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guides who are guided."

Longing carries the one who longs to striving in the journey toward his Beloved, makes the path near for him, folds the distance for him, and eases for him pains and hardships. It is among the greatest blessings Allah bestows upon His servant. But for this blessing there are sayings and deeds which are the means by which it is attained. Allah the Glorified hears those sayings and knows those deeds, and He knows who is fit for this blessing, who gives thanks for it, recognizes its worth and loves the One who bestowed it, so this blessing is pleasing to Him and he is made good by it, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We tried some of them with others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53]. So whenever a blessing from the blessings of his Lord escapes the servant, let him recite to himself: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

Then He consoled them with another consolation, namely that their striving in it is only for their own selves, its fruit returns to them, and He is free of need from the worlds. The benefit of this striving returns to them, not to Him, the Glorified. Then He informed them that by their striving and their faith He will admit them into the company of the righteous.

Then He informed about the state of one who enters faith without insight, and that if he is harmed for Allah's sake, he regards the people's trial of him as Allah's punishment, meaning their harm to him and their inflicting upon him what is disliked and painful, which the Messengers and their followers must suffer from those who oppose them. He takes this, in his fleeing from them and abandoning the cause that brought him the harm, to be like the punishment of Allah, from which the believers fled by means of faith. The believers, out of the perfection of their insight, fled from the pain of Allah's punishment to faith, and bore what is in it of passing pain that soon departs. But this one, out of weakness of insight, fled from the pain of the punishment of the enemies of the Messengers to conformity with them and following them, so he fled from the pain of their punishment into the pain of Allah's punishment. Thus he made the pain of the people's trial, in fleeing from it, equal to the pain of Allah's punishment, and he was utterly deceived, for he sought refuge from the scorching sand in the fire, and fled from the pain of an hour into the pain of eternity. And when Allah grants victory to His army and His friends, he says: "Indeed, I was with you," and Allah knows best what his breast conceals of hypocrisy.

The purpose is this: Allah the Glorified, by His wisdom, necessarily tests and tries souls, so that through the test He makes evident the good from the bad, and who is fit for His friendship and honors and who is not, and in order to purify the souls that are fit for Him and to refine them through the furnace of testing, like gold, which does not become pure or free of its dross except through testing. For the soul is originally ignorant and wrongdoing, and it has acquired through ignorance and wrongdoing a corruption whose removal requires smelting and refining. If it comes out clean in this abode, well; otherwise, it is in the furnace of Hell. When the servant is refined and purified, he is permitted to enter Paradise.

(Benefit)
Trial is the furnace of hearts and the touchstone of faith, and through it the truthful is distinguished from the liar. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 3]

Trial divides people into truthful and liar, believer and hypocrite, and good and bad. Whoever endures it, it becomes a mercy for him, and by his patience he is saved from a greater trial than it; and whoever does not endure it falls into a trial worse than it.

(Section)

Ibn al-Qayyim said in (Shifa' al-'Alil):
Know that the best and greatest of gifts, absolutely, is faith and its reward, and this is not realized except through testing and examination. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars. Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is their judgment. Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah – then indeed, the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds.﴾

In this surah He, the Glorified, mentioned that He necessarily tests His creation and tries them, so that the truthful is distinguished from the liar, the believer from the disbeliever, and the one who thanks Him and worships Him from the one who disbelieves in Him, turns away from Him and worships other than Him. He mentioned the conditions of those being tested in the immediate and the deferred, and mentioned the leaders of those tested in this world, namely the Messengers and their followers, and the outcome of their affair and what they came to. He opened with a rebuke against whoever thinks he can escape testing and trial in this abode when he claims faith, and that His wisdom and His dealings with His creation refuse that. He informed about the secret of this trial and ordeal, which is making evident the truthful from the liar and the believer from the disbeliever. He, the Glorified, knew this before it occurred, but His justice and praiseworthiness required that He not requite the servants merely by His knowledge of them, but by what is known when it is found and realized. The trial is what brought it out and into existence, and then it became fitting for the requital to fall upon it.

Then He, the Glorified, denounced whoever does not commit to faith in Him and to following His messengers out of fear of the trial and ordeal by which His messengers and their followers are tested, supposing and reckoning that by turning away from faith and from believing His messengers he escapes the trial and ordeal. For before him lies trial, ordeal and punishment greater and more grievous than what he fled from.

For after the sending of messengers to people, the accountable stand between two matters:
either one of them says, "I believe," or he does not say so but persists in evil deeds.

Whoever says, "We believe," his Lord, the Exalted, tests and tries him, so that the reality of his faith, its evidence and his steadfastness upon it may be established, and that it is not a faith of mere ease and prosperity but a faith that is firm in both states of blessing and affliction.

Whoever does not believe should not suppose that he can frustrate or escape the Lord, the Exalted. Rather, he is in His grip, and his forelock is in His hand. So he will suffer a greater trial than the one suffered by the one who says, "I have believed." Whoever believes in Him and His messengers will inevitably be tested by his enemies and the enemies of His messengers with what pains him and burdens him. Whoever does not believe in Him and His messengers will inevitably be punished, and he will suffer pain and hardship many times greater than the pain of the believers. Pain is therefore inevitable for every soul, whether believing or disbelieving. But the believer experiences pain in this world more intensely, and then it ends and is followed by the greatest pleasure. The disbeliever experiences pleasure and delight at first, and then it ends and is followed by the greatest pain and hardship.

This is also the condition of those who follow their desires: they take pleasure in them at first, and then pains follow in proportion to what they obtained from them. And those who refrain from them gain, by their loss, at first, and then pain is followed by pleasure and delight in proportion to what they refrained from and abandoned. So pain and pleasure are a necessity for every human being. But the difference between the small, transient, immediate and the great, enduring, deferred is vast. This is why the distinctive trait of reason is to consider consequences and final ends. Whoever thinks that he can free himself from pain such that it never touches him at all, his thought is the most false of falsehoods. For man is created exposed to pleasure and pain, joy and sorrow, delight and grief. This comes from two aspects: from his composition, nature and constitution, for he is composed of humors that are varied and opposed, whose balance is impossible or very difficult to achieve in every respect; rather, some of them must inevitably transgress against others and depart from the limit of balance, so pain arises. And from his fellow-human beings, for he is naturally social, unable to live alone, and cannot live except with them. He and they have pleasures and aims that are opposed and conflicting, and they cannot be combined; rather, when one of them is attained, others are lost. He wants them to agree with his aims and will, and they want the same from him. If he agrees with them, he suffers pain and hardship in proportion to what he has lost of his own will. If he does not agree with them, they harm him, torment him, and strive to nullify his aims, just as he did not agree with their aims. So he suffers pain and torment accordingly. He is therefore in pain, hardship and toil, whether he agrees with them or opposes them. This is especially so when their agreement is upon matters that he knows to be false beliefs, corrupt wills and deeds that harm him in their consequences. In agreeing with them there is the greatest pain, and in opposing them there is the arising of pain. So reason, religion, manliness and knowledge command him to bear the lesser of two pains, in order to be freed from the greater, and to prefer the transient of the two so as to be saved from the enduring and continuous one.

Whoever supports the criminal oppressors in their oppression, or the people of whims and innovations in their whims and innovations, or the people of immorality and desires in their immorality and desires, in order to be freed by supporting them from the pain of their harm, will suffer from agreeing with them, both immediately and in the future, many times more than what he fled from. It is God's custom with His creation that He punishes them for their faith and their support of them, even if he endures the pain of opposing them and keeping away from them. That endurance will bring him an immediate and future pleasure that exceeds the pleasure of agreement by manifold. It is God's custom with His creation that He raises him above them and humiliates them through him, in proportion to his patience, piety, trust in Him and sincerity. If the pain and punishment are of this kind, then in God and in seeking His good pleasure and following His messengers, it is more fitting and more beneficial than in pursuing people's pleasure, their approval and fulfilling their aims. Since the time of pain and punishment is long, his patience is long: his breaths are hours, his hours are days, his days are months and years. God, the Exalted, tested them in it by informing them that this trial is deferred and then will end. He set for its people a term for meeting Him, to console them with it, to comfort their souls, and to make its burdens light for them. He said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with God, then the term of God is surely coming; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

So when the servant contemplates the term of that trial and its ending, and the term of meeting Him, the Tester, the Exalted, and its affirmation, what he is in becomes easy for him and its burden becomes light. Then, since that cannot be achieved except through striving against the self, against Satan, and against his fellow human beings, and since the worker who knows that the fruit of his knowledge and his toil returns to him alone, without anyone else thanking him for it, makes his effort more complete and his striving more abundant, God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself; surely God is Self-Sufficient above the worlds.﴾ Also, no one should imagine that the benefit of this striving, patience and endurance returns to God, the Exalted, for He is independent of the worlds. He did not command them with what He commanded out of any need for them, nor forbid them from what He forbade out of stinginess towards them. Rather, He commanded them with what returns benefit and welfare to them in their livelihood and their hereafter, and forbade them from what returns harm and ruin to them in their livelihood and their hereafter. So the fruit of this trial and testing is specific to them. His wisdom required that He establish this as a decreed cause to distinguish the wicked from the good, the miserable from the misguided, and who is fit for it from who is not fit. He said: ﴿God would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾ So God, the Exalted, tested them by sending messengers to them with His commands and prohibitions and His choosing. Thus, by His messengers, their good was distinguished from their wicked, and their excellent from their inferior. Reward and punishment then fell upon a known matter that this trial and testing made manifest.

Then, since the one being tested must inevitably deviate from the path of patience and striving, due to the impulses of his nature, his desire, and his weakness in resisting what he was tested with, the Exalted promised that He would overlook that for him and expiate it, because when he was commanded and bound himself to obedience, His mercy required that He expiate his misdeeds and reward him with the best of his deeds. Then the Exalted mentioned the servant's trial with his parents, and what he was commanded regarding obeying them, and his patience in striving against them that he should not associate anything with Him. So he should be patient in this ordeal and tribulation and not obey them, but accompany them in this state with kindness, and turn away from them to follow the way of His messengers. In turning away from them and their way, and turning towards those who oppose them and towards His way, there is a test and trial with what it contains. Then the Exalted mentioned the condition of one who entered faith with weak resolve, little patience, and no steadfastness under the ordeal and trial. When he is harmed for God, as the custom of God is and as His wisdom requires in testing His friends through His enemies and giving them power over them with various kinds of hardship and harm, he does not endure that; he panics, flees from it, and from its causes, as one flees from the punishment of God. So He made the people's persecution of him for faith and obedience to His messengers like the punishment of God for whoever punishes him for associating partners with God and opposing His messengers. This indicates lack of insight, and that faith has not entered his heart nor has he tasted its sweetness, to the point that he equated God's punishment of him for faith in God and His messenger with God's punishment of whoever does not believe in Him and His messengers. This is the condition of one who worships God on an edge, whose foot has not been firmly planted in faith and the worship of God. He is among the tested and tormented, even if he escapes the people's punishment of him for faith. Then He mentioned the condition of this person at the time of the victory of the believers, that when they are granted victory he comes to them and says, "I was with you," while God knows what his heart conceals contrary to his words.

Then the Exalted mentioned the trial of Noah with his people for nine hundred and fifty years, and the trial of his people with obedience to him, so they denied him, and He tested them with the flood, then after that with the storm. Then He mentioned the trial of Abraham with his people, and how they rejected him, and He tested them with obeying and following him. Then He mentioned the trial of Lot with his people, and their trial with him, and what his affair and theirs came to. Then He mentioned the trial of Shu'ayb with his people, and their trial with him, and what their state and his came to. Then He mentioned what He tested 'Ad and Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh, Haman and their armies with, of faith in Him and worshipping Him alone, then the various punishments with which He tested them. Then He mentioned the trial of His messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with various kinds of disbelievers, from idolaters and People of the Book, and commanded him to argue with the People of the Book in the best manner. Then He commanded His servants who were tested by His enemies to migrate from their land to His vast land, to worship Him there. Then He alerted them, through the greater migration from the abode of this world to the abode of the Hereafter, to their lesser migration from land to land, and informed them that their return is to Him, so there is no settled dwelling for them in this abode apart from meeting Him. Then He explained to them the condition of those who are patient in the trial for Him: that He will settle them in gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. So He consoled them for the land and home they left for His sake, which had been their dwelling, by settling them in a home better than it, more gathering of every good, pleasure and bliss, with eternal immortality, and that this is by their patience in the trial and their trust in their Lord. Then He informed them that He guarantees their provision in other than their land, just as He provided for them in their land. So they should not worry about carrying their provision: how many a creature travels from place to place without carrying its provision. Then He informed them that the period of trial and testing in this abode is very short compared with the abode of life and permanence. Then the Exalted mentioned the end of the people of trial who did not believe in Him, that their stay in this abode is enjoyment, and that they will know, at their removal from it, what they missed of the lasting bliss and what they gained of painful punishment. And He mentioned the end of the people of trial who believed in Him, obeyed His messengers, and strove against their selves and their enemy in the abode of trial, what He guides and helps them to. So the Exalted informed that the greatest of His gifts and its most excellent, in this world and the Hereafter, belongs to the people of trial who were patient under His trial and trusted in Him, and He informed that the greatest and most grievous of His punishment belongs to those who were not patient under His trial, fled from it, and preferred immediate comfort over it.

So the content of this surah is the secret of creation and command, for it is the surah of trial and testing, and the explanation of the condition of the people of affliction in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever reflects on its opening, its middle and its end will find within it that the beginning of the matter is trial and testing, its middle is patience and trust, and its end is guidance and victory. And God is the One sought for help, which clarifies it.

Allah the Glorified hears those sayings and knows those deeds, and He knows who is fit for this blessing, who gives thanks for it, recognizes its worth and loves the One who bestowed it, so this blessing is pleasing to Him and he is made good by it, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We tried some of them with others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53]. So whenever a blessing from the blessings of his Lord escapes the servant, let him recite to himself: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

Then He consoled them with another consolation, namely that their striving in it is only for their own selves, its fruit returns to them, and He is free of need from the worlds. The benefit of this striving returns to them, not to Him, the Glorified. Then He informed them that by their striving and their faith He will admit them into the company of the righteous.

Then He informed about the state of one who enters faith without insight, and that if he is harmed for Allah's sake, he regards the people's trial of him as Allah's punishment, meaning their harm to him and their inflicting upon him what is disliked and painful, which the Messengers and their followers must suffer from those who oppose them. He takes this, in his fleeing from them and abandoning the cause that brought him the harm, to be like the punishment of Allah, from which the believers fled by means of faith. The believers, out of the perfection of their insight, fled from the pain of Allah's punishment to faith, and bore what is in it of passing pain that soon departs. But this one, out of weakness of insight, fled from the pain of the punishment of the enemies of the Messengers to conformity with them and following them, so he fled from the pain of their punishment into the pain of Allah's punishment. Thus he made the pain of the people's trial, in fleeing from it, equal to the pain of Allah's punishment, and he was utterly deceived, for he sought refuge from the scorching sand in the fire, and fled from the pain of an hour into the pain of eternity. And when Allah grants victory to His army and His friends, he says: "Indeed, I was with you," and Allah knows best what his breast conceals of hypocrisy.

The purpose is this: Allah the Glorified, by His wisdom, necessarily tests and tries souls, so that through the test He makes evident the good from the bad, and who is fit for His friendship and honors and who is not, and in order to purify the souls that are fit for Him and to refine them through the furnace of testing, like gold, which does not become pure or free of its dross except through testing. For the soul is originally ignorant and wrongdoing, and it has acquired through ignorance and wrongdoing a corruption whose removal requires smelting and refining. If it comes out clean in this abode, well; otherwise, it is in the furnace of Hell. When the servant is refined and purified, he is permitted to enter Paradise.

(Benefit)
Trial is the furnace of hearts and the touchstone of faith, and through it the truthful is distinguished from the liar. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 3]

(Section)

Ibn al-Qayyim said in (Shifa' al-'Alil):
Know that the best and greatest of gifts, absolutely, is faith and its reward, and this is not realized except through testing and examination. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars. Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is their judgment. Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah – then indeed, the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds.﴾

In this surah He, the Glorified, mentioned that He necessarily tests His creation and tries them, so that the truthful is distinguished from the liar, the believer from the disbeliever, and the one who thanks Him and worships Him from the one who disbelieves in Him, turns away from Him and worships other than Him. He mentioned the conditions of those being tested in the immediate and the deferred, and mentioned the leaders of those tested in this world, namely the Messengers and their followers, and the outcome of their affair and what they came to. He opened with a rebuke against whoever thinks he can escape testing and trial in this abode when he claims faith, and that His wisdom and His dealings with His creation refuse that. He informed about the secret of this trial and ordeal, which is making evident the truthful from the liar and the believer from the disbeliever. He, the Glorified, knew this before it occurred, but His justice and praiseworthiness required that He not requite the servants merely by His knowledge of them, but by what is known when it is found and realized. The trial is what brought it out and into existence, and then it became fitting for the requital to fall upon it.

Then He, the Glorified, denounced whoever does not commit to faith in Him and to following His messengers out of fear of the trial and ordeal by which His messengers and their followers are tested, supposing and reckoning that by turning away from faith and from believing His messengers he escapes the trial and ordeal. For before him lies trial, ordeal and punishment greater and more grievous than what he fled from.

For after the sending of messengers to people, the accountable stand between two matters:
either one of them says, "I believe," or he does not say so but persists in evil deeds.

Whoever says, "We believe," his Lord, the Exalted, tests and tries him, so that the reality of his faith, its evidence and his steadfastness upon it may be established, and that it is not a faith of mere ease and prosperity but a faith that is firm in both states of blessing and affliction.

Whoever does not believe should not suppose that he can frustrate or escape the Lord, the Exalted. Rather, he is in His grip, and his forelock is in His hand. So he will suffer a greater trial than the one suffered by the one who says, "I have believed." Whoever believes in Him and His messengers will inevitably be tested by his enemies and the enemies of His messengers with what pains him and burdens him. Whoever does not believe in Him and His messengers will inevitably be punished, and he will suffer pain and hardship many times greater than the pain of the believers. Pain is therefore inevitable for every soul, whether believing or disbelieving. But the believer experiences pain in this world more intensely, and then it ends and is followed by the greatest pleasure. The disbeliever experiences pleasure and delight at first, and then it ends and is followed by the greatest pain and hardship.

This is also the condition of those who follow their desires: they take pleasure in them at first, and then pains follow in proportion to what they obtained from them. And those who refrain from them gain, by their loss, at first, and then pain is followed by pleasure and delight in proportion to what they refrained from and abandoned. So pain and pleasure are a necessity for every human being. But the difference between the small, transient, immediate and the great, enduring, deferred is vast. This is why the distinctive trait of reason is to consider consequences and final ends. Whoever thinks that he can free himself from pain such that it never touches him at all, his thought is the most false of falsehoods. For man is created exposed to pleasure and pain, joy and sorrow, delight and grief. This comes from two aspects: from his composition, nature and constitution, for he is composed of humors that are varied and opposed, whose balance is impossible or very difficult to achieve in every respect; rather, some of them must inevitably transgress against others and depart from the limit of balance, so pain arises. And from his fellow-human beings, for he is naturally social, unable to live alone, and cannot live except with them. He and they have pleasures and aims that are opposed and conflicting, and they cannot be combined; rather, when one of them is attained, others are lost. He wants them to agree with his aims and will, and they want the same from him. If he agrees with them, he suffers pain and hardship in proportion to what he has lost of his own will. If he does not agree with them, they harm him, torment him, and strive to nullify his aims, just as he did not agree with their aims. So he suffers pain and torment accordingly. He is therefore in pain, hardship and toil, whether he agrees with them or opposes them. This is especially so when their agreement is upon matters that he knows to be false beliefs, corrupt wills and deeds that harm him in their consequences. In agreeing with them there is the greatest pain, and in opposing them there is the arising of pain. So reason, religion, manliness and knowledge command him to bear the lesser of two pains, in order to be freed from the greater, and to prefer the transient of the two so as to be saved from the enduring and continuous one.

Whoever supports the criminal oppressors in their oppression, or the people of whims and innovations in their whims and innovations, or the people of immorality and desires in their immorality and desires, in order to be freed by supporting them from the pain of their harm, will suffer from agreeing with them, both immediately and in the future, many times more than what he fled from. It is God's custom with His creation that He punishes them for their faith and their support of them, even if he endures the pain of opposing them and keeping away from them. That endurance will bring him an immediate and future pleasure that exceeds the pleasure of agreement by manifold. It is God's custom with His creation that He raises him above them and humiliates them through him, in proportion to his patience, piety, trust in Him and sincerity. If the pain and punishment are of this kind, then in God and in seeking His good pleasure and following His messengers, it is more fitting and more beneficial than in pursuing people's pleasure, their approval and fulfilling their aims. Since the time of pain and punishment is long, his patience is long: his breaths are hours, his hours are days, his days are months and years. God, the Exalted, tested them in it by informing them that this trial is deferred and then will end. He set for its people a term for meeting Him, to console them with it, to comfort their souls, and to make its burdens light for them. He said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with God, then the term of God is surely coming; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

So when the servant contemplates the term of that trial and its ending, and the term of meeting Him, the Tester, the Exalted, and its affirmation, what he is in becomes easy for him and its burden becomes light. Then, since that cannot be achieved except through striving against the self, against Satan, and against his fellow human beings, and since the worker who knows that the fruit of his knowledge and his toil returns to him alone, without anyone else thanking him for it, makes his effort more complete and his striving more abundant, God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself; surely God is Self-Sufficient above the worlds.﴾ Also, no one should imagine that the benefit of this striving, patience and endurance returns to God, the Exalted, for He is independent of the worlds. He did not command them with what He commanded out of any need for them, nor forbid them from what He forbade out of stinginess towards them. Rather, He commanded them with what returns benefit and welfare to them in their livelihood and their hereafter, and forbade them from what returns harm and ruin to them in their livelihood and their hereafter. So the fruit of this trial and testing is specific to them. His wisdom required that He establish this as a decreed cause to distinguish the wicked from the good, the miserable from the misguided, and who is fit for it from who is not fit. Then He mentioned the trial of Lot with his people, and their trial with him, and what his affair and theirs came to. Then He mentioned the trial of Shu'ayb with his people, and their trial with him, and what their state and his came to. Then He mentioned what He tested 'Ad and Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh, Haman and their armies with, of faith in Him and worshipping Him alone, then the various punishments with which He tested them. Then He mentioned the trial of His messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with various kinds of disbelievers, from idolaters and People of the Book, and commanded him to argue with the People of the Book in the best manner. Then He commanded His servants who were tested by His enemies to migrate from their land to His vast land, to worship Him there. Then He alerted them, through the greater migration from the abode of this world to the abode of the Hereafter, to their lesser migration from land to land, and informed them that their return is to Him, so there is no settled dwelling for them in this abode apart from meeting Him. Then He explained to them the condition of those who are patient in the trial for Him: that He will settle them in gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. So He consoled them for the land and home they left for His sake, which had been their dwelling, by settling them in a home better than it, more gathering of every good, pleasure and bliss, with eternal immortality, and that this is by their patience in the trial and their trust in their Lord. Then He informed them that He guarantees their provision in other than their land, just as He provided for them in their land. So they should not worry about carrying their provision: how many a creature travels from place to place without carrying its provision. Then He informed them that the period of trial and testing in this abode is very short compared with the abode of life and permanence. Then the Exalted mentioned the end of the people of trial who did not believe in Him, that their stay in this abode is enjoyment, and that they will know, at their removal from it, what they missed of the lasting bliss and what they gained of painful punishment. And He mentioned the end of the people of trial who believed in Him, obeyed His messengers, and strove against their selves and their enemy in the abode of trial, what He guides and helps them to. So the Exalted informed that the greatest of His gifts and its most excellent, in this world and the Hereafter, belongs to the people of trial who were patient under His trial and trusted in Him, and He informed that the greatest and most grievous of His punishment belongs to those who were not patient under His trial, fled from it, and preferred immediate comfort over it.

So the content of this surah is the secret of creation and command, for it is the surah of trial and testing, and the explanation of the condition of the people of affliction in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever reflects on its opening, its middle and its end will find within it that the beginning of the matter is trial and testing, its middle is patience and trust, and its end is guidance and victory. And God is the One sought for help, which clarifies it.

(Section)

Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds. And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do. And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous. Whoever says, "We believe," his Lord tests him, tries him and puts him to trial. Fitnah (trial, testing) is affliction and examination, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liar. Whoever does not say, "We believe," let him not think that he can frustrate Allah, escape Him or outpace Him, for he is only folding the stages in His hands.

[Poetry]
And how can a man flee from Him in his sin,
When the stages are being folded in His hands?

Whoever believes in the messengers and obeys them, their enemies oppose him and harm him, so he is afflicted with what pains him. Therefore, every soul that believes or turns away from belief must experience pain. But the believer experiences pain in this world at the outset, and then the good outcome is his in this world and the Hereafter. The one who turns away from belief experiences pleasure at the outset, and then he proceeds to lasting pain.

al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked: Which is better for a man, that he be empowered or that he be tested? He said: He is not empowered until he is tested, and Allah the Exalted tested the Messengers of firm resolve, and when they were patient, He empowered them. So no one should think that he will be free of pain at all. Rather, the people of pain differ in their intellect: the most intelligent of them is the one who sells lasting great pain for brief, passing pain, and the most wretched of them is the one who sells brief, passing pain for lasting great pain.

If it is said: How would a sensible person choose this? It is said: What drives him to this is ready cash versus deferred payment.

And the soul is entrusted with love of what is immediate.
﴿Nay, but you love the immediate and neglect the Hereafter.﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 20] ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate and leave behind them a heavy day.﴾ [al-Insan: 27] This occurs to everyone, for man is civil by nature; he must live among people, and people have wills and perceptions, so they ask him to agree with them in them. If he does not agree with them, they harm him and punish him; and if he agrees with them, harm and punishment befall him, sometimes from them and sometimes from others. Like one who has religion and piety who dwells among wicked, oppressive people, who cannot carry out their wickedness and oppression except with his agreement or his silence. If he agrees with them or remains silent, he is safe from their evil at the outset, but then they dominate him with humiliation and harm many times over what he feared at the outset had he denounced them and opposed them. And if he is safe from them, he must still be humiliated and punished at the hands of others. So the utmost prudence lies in acting upon what 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, said to Mu'awiyah:

Whoever reflects on the conditions of the world will see this often: among those who help rulers in their corrupt aims, and among those who help people of innovation in their innovations, fleeing from their punishment. Whomever Allah guides, inspires with his right guidance and protects from the evil of his own self, refrains from agreeing to the commission of what is forbidden, and endures their hostility. Indeed, longing for His meeting may sometimes make him forget witnessing the pain and feeling it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his Lord for longing for His meeting, saying in the supplication narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Hibban: "O Allah, I ask You by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive if life is good for me, and take me when death is good for me. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guides who are guided."
